merger_description:
Salsa Bidco, Inc., an acquisition vehicle wholly owned by the Eighth Cinven Fund which is indirectly managed and controlled by Cinven Limited (**Cinven**), proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Salsify, Inc. (**Salsify**) (the **Acquisition**).

Cinven is a private equity firm engaged in the provision of investment management and advisory services to a number of investment funds. The controlled companies in Cinven’s portfolio of investments are active in a variety of sectors, including business services, consumer, financial services, healthcare, industrials, technology, media, and telecommunications. Cinven has exclusive authority to make investment and management decisions for the Eighth Cinven Fund.

Salsify is a US-headquartered provider of cloud-native product experience management software solutions. Salsify’s platform is used by consumer goods manufacturers, retailers and distributors as a centralised product data repository, enabling them to manage and distribute product content across digital commerce channels.

determination_table_content.details:
Salsa Bidco, Inc., an acquisition vehicle wholly owned by the Eighth
Cinven Fund which is indirectly managed and controlled by Cinven
Limited (Cinven), applied for a notification waiver in respect of its
proposed acquisition of 100% of the shares in Salsify, Inc. (Salsify),
as described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Cinven, is a private equity firm engaged in the provision
of investment management and advisory services to a number of
investment funds. The controlled companies in Cinven’s portfolio of
investments are active in a variety of sectors, including business
services, consumer, financial services, healthcare, industrials,
technology, media, and telecommunications. Cinven has exclusive
authority to make investment and management decisions for the
Eighth Cinven Fund.
The target, Salsify, is a US-headquartered provider of cloud-native
product experience management software solutions. Salsify’s
platform is used by consumer goods manufacturers, retailers, and
distributors as a centralised product data repository, enabling them
to manage and distribute product content across digital commerce
channels.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. There is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationship
between Cinven or its controlled portfolio companies and Salsify in
Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
